Atomic Chat

Local AI app and inference engine for agents. Run open-weight LLMs locally — private, on your machine.

  
  
  
  
  
 

Getting Started · Hugging Face · Discord · X / Twitter · Bug Reports

 
 
 

---

 📦 Download

 Desktop 
 
  
  
 
 

 Linux packages — from the Atomic Chat repository, updated by your package manager ( how to install ) 
 
  
  
 
 

 Mobile 
 
  
 
 

---

 🔌 Use It as an API

Atomic Chat runs an OpenAI-compatible server at — a drop-in replacement for the OpenAI SDK. Load a model in the app, then point any client at it:

 

 

Bound to 127.0.0.1 by default; set host: 0.0.0.0 to expose it on your LAN. Works with any agent, CLI, or IDE plugin that speaks the OpenAI API — see Launch With below.

---

 ✨ Features

 Local models 

- Run open-weight LLMs locally from HuggingFace — Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, and others
- Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative decoding — 30–70% throughput boost on supported models, up to 3× on Gemma 4
- DFlash block-diffusion decoding — up to 6× faster on Qwen 3.6, Gemma 4, Kimi K2.5
- Flash Attention toggle ( on / off / auto )
- Automatic reasoning-context tracking for chain-of-thought models
- Auto context-window expansion with overflow notifications
- EAGLE-3 speculative decoding for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon (MLX)
- MTP on MLX for Qwen 3.5 / 3.6 and DeepSeek V4
- TurboQuant KV cache ( turbo3 / turbo4 ) on llama.cpp — now on Windows & Linux too, not just macOS: up to 4.3× smaller KV cache footprint, CPU and GPU (CUDA / Vulkan)
- TurboQuant KV cache on MLX-VLM — smaller memory footprint via RHT-correct fast paths

 Cloud models 

- Built-in providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq, MiniMax, Qwen, Moonshot
- Bring your own key, switch model per chat, mix local and cloud freely

 Tools & integrations 

- One-click agent launch — launch agents like Atomic Agent, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cline, OpenCode, Droid, Goose, OpenHands, Copilot CLI, Kilo Code, Zed and ZCode in one click from the Integrations tab
- Artifacts — live preview panel for HTML/CSS/JS code with copy, download and print
- Connect multiple MCP servers — bring your own tools, file access, web search
- Custom assistants with per-assistant system prompts
- Projects with conversation tree view in the sidebar

 Local API 

- OpenAI-compatible server at — drop-in replacement for the OpenAI SDK
- Works with any agent, CLI, or IDE plugin that speaks the OpenAI API
- Bound to 127.0.0.1 by default; set host: 0.0.0.0 to expose on LAN

 Privacy 

- Everything runs locally when you want it to — local server is loopback-only by default
- Your conversations and keys stay on your machine

---

 ⚙️ Inference Engines

Twelve engines under the hood, all exposed through one OpenAI-compatible API at Each shows up as a provider only where it can run; the ones that need a download install from Settings → Providers in one click.

 Text and vision models 

 Engine What it runs Where 
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------- 
 Upstream llama.cpp GGUF models; the official ggml-org build, with MTP. The default engine on Windows and Linux for the widest hardware coverage. macOS, Windows, Linux — CPU, Metal, CUDA, Vulkan 
 atomic-llama-cpp-turboquant GGUF models on our llama.cpp fork with TurboQuant KV cache ( turbo3 / turbo4 ) for faster, lower-memory quantized inference ("Atomic Llama.cpp Turboquant"). macOS, Windows, Linux — CPU, Metal, CUDA, Vulkan 
 PrismML llama.cpp PrismML's Bonsai models, whose 1- and 2-bit tensor types the other llama.cpp builds don't load. macOS, Windows x64, Linux x64 — CPU, Metal, CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm 
 MLX-VLM MLX models, vision-language included, with DFlash, EAGLE-3 and MTP. Faster than llama.cpp on M-series chips for supported models. macOS on Apple Silicon 
 Apple Foundation Models Apple's on-device model, nothing to download. macOS 26+ with Apple Intelligence enabled 
 Foundry Local Microsoft's ONNX models on the CPU, GPU or NPU. Windows x64 and arm64, macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon, Linux 
 LiteRT-LM Google's on-device .litertlm models (Gemma and others), with the Intel NPU through OpenVINO on Windows. macOS 12+ on Apple Silicon, Windows x64, Linux 
 GenieX Qualcomm's runtime for Snapdragon: GGUF models on the Hexagon NPU, Adreno GPU or CPU, and Qualcomm AI Hub bundles on the NPU. Windows on Snapdragon X (X Elite, X Plus, X, X2 Elite, X2 Plus) 
 FastFlowLM Local text models on AMD XDNA2, installed from the shared catalog with pinned files and hashes. Windows 11 x64, Linux x64 with a prepared AMD XDNA2 NPU 
 TensorRT-LLM NVIDIA's high-throughput server for Hugging Face checkpoints. Linux, and Windows x64 through WSL 2 — NVIDIA GPU 
 vLLM Hugging Face checkpoints on vLLM's server. Linux, and Windows x64 through WSL 2 — NVIDIA GPU 
 SGLang Hugging Face checkpoints on SGLang's server. Linux, and Windows x64 through WSL 2 — NVIDIA GPU 

TensorRT-LLM, vLLM and SGLang run in a container that Atomic Chat sets up and manages itself; on Windows it lives in Atomic Chat's own WSL distribution.

 Images and video 

 Engine What it runs Where 
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 stable-diffusion.cpp (our build) Images (FLUX, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, Krea) and video (Wan 2.2, LTX-2), in the Images and Videos tabs. macOS on Apple Silicon, Windows, Linux — CPU, Metal, CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm
